summary: Round 4, scoped to the delta since a351aa9e. Both round-3 minors are genuinely closed, verified by mutation in my own tree rather than accepted. (1) The per-request pointer PUT now DIES for the right reason: capturing requests.size() in CheckpointWriter.capture and looping the pointer PUT over it fails thePointerADVANCESAndIsWrittenExactlyOncePerTrigger with 'Expected size: 2 but was: 3', at CheckpointDiscoveryTest.java:205, under the correct .as() label -- not an unrelated failure and not a compile error. (2) The other two thirds of that label are supported too, which I did not take on trust: a pointer PUT looped over pods.keySet() fails 4 vs 2, and one looped over pendingStreams.keySet() fails 4 vs 2. All three dimensions are now real. (3) The batching does NOT produce two deltas -- a temporary assertion in my tree confirmed two commitAll calls produce exactly two .delta PUTs and two .ckpt PUTs, so the K trigger fires once per commitAll and the size-2 assertion passes for the right reason; CommitLog.commitAll issues a single putIfAbsent(keyFor(nextSequence)) per call, one delta however many requests it batches. (4) The distinct pod ids (pod + request) and distinct segment keys change nothing any other test observes: theWriterMAINTAINSThePointerSoDiscoveryFindsWhatItJustWrote builds its own CommitRequest list with pod 'poda' and never calls the helper, so its containsEntry("poda", 7L) is untouched; the three other commitOne callers pass requests=1 and assert only on pointer keys, sequences or Invariants, never on pod names. (5) tickAndAwait's restored paragraph matches the production it guards -- CheckpointWriter.tickForever increments ticksProcessed AFTER the work, so rendezvousing on the counter rather than on tick() returning is correct and the comment says why. (6) Rules 4-5: no assertion was weakened anywhere in the delta. The only non-helper test change is a corrected comment in CheckpointWriterContentTest.theCheckpointKeyIsZeroPaddedSoLexicographicOrderIsNumericOrder; its three assertions are byte-identical, and hasSize(2) held constant while the fixture's workload GREW, which is a strengthening. I also re-ran three mutants from my earlier rounds to confirm they stay dead against this hash: the reader's epoch hardcoded to 1 fails two tests, the pointer's put weakened to putIfAbsent fails thePointerADVANCES, and the writer's pointer epoch hardcoded to 1 fails theWriterPutsThePointerUnderITSOwnEpochsPrefix. Full ./gradlew test green in my tree; staged diff left at d3635616ea225718907b2a3889b4dc30bdba61ed49ad0c49a1d88e57e5a0f807, unchanged.
